transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood, AE); Liam O'Connell (Redwood, SE); Priya Menon (Atlas, Head of Security); Jared Kim (Atlas, Platform Engineer); Sofia Alvarez (Atlas, Compliance)

Summary: Quick posture review focused on evidence access, RBAC & SSO mapping, and KMS/BYOK options for Atlas Ventures' upcoming SOC 2 Type II window. Agreed next steps around Trust Center access and a small KMS integration test.

Topics: trust center access; SOC 2 / ISO attestation; RBAC mapping and service accounts; SSO/SAML metadata; audit log retention and ingestion; encryption (KMS/HSM, BYOK); data residency concerns.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for squeezing this in. Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. Quick intros?
[00:07] Priya Menon: Priya, head of security at Atlas. We have... um, primary focus is on the SOC 2 window coming in Q3, so wanna make sure access to evidence is smooth.
[00:13] Jared Kim: Jared, platform eng, I own deployment and logging pipelines.
[00:16] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia, compliance, will be coordinating auditors and evidence.
[00:19] Liam O'Connell: Liam from Redwood, SE — I'll be the deep-dive person on the KMS and logging side.

[02:05] Priya: Cool. So, high level question — how do we get read-only access to the Trust Center? We're used to a shared bucket or a portal with RBAC and time-limited links.
[02:18] Maya: Yeah. We can invite your compliance group as read-only to our Trust Center. It's role-based — you can limit to "evidence viewer" and restrict by org unit. We also provide signed URLs for bulk evidence download.
[02:32] Sofia: Are those signed URLs expiring? Our auditors typically want a copy, sometimes we need a mirror for retention policies.
[02:38] Maya: Signed URLs are expiring by default but we can provision time-limited windows and an export package. We'll also keep a long-term retention copy in the Trust Center for entitlements, but we can coordinate export for your legal needs.

[05:00] Jared: On RBAC — we're trying to map our internal roles to Redwood roles. We use SAML SSO with Okta. How granular is your role model? Can we map service accounts separately from human users?
[05:12] Liam: Yes. Redwood supports SAML SSO with role attribute mappings. You can map groups in Okta to Redwood roles (admin, operator, auditor, viewer). Service accounts can be represented as separate identities — we recommend using machine accounts with scoped permissions and short-lived tokens.
[05:30] Jared: Short-lived tokens — are those rotated automatically?
[05:33] Liam: Tokens are ephemeral by default for service calls; we also support customer-managed keys for encryption and support for BYOK flows — which I'll detail in a sec.

[07:10] Priya: Audit logs — what level of detail do you keep? We need user, action, resource, timestamp, and IP+region ideally. Also chain-of-custody for evidence.
[07:22] Liam: Our audit stream includes actor principal, action verb, target resource identifier, timestamps, region, and request metadata including source IP. For private deployments we can forward logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog/ELK). For hosted we keep a 365-day primary retention and can export. There is sometimes a mismatch in field names — the transcript has K-V cache referenced as KV cache, sometimes transcribed weirdly — but the log schema is documented in the Trust Center.
[07:50] Sofia: 365 days — for SOC2 our auditors asked for 12 months minimum, sometimes 24 months. Is that configurable?
[07:57] Liam: Hosted default is 365, but we offer longer retention as an add-on. For Dedicated or Private installs you can control retention to match 24 months. We'll note this as a requirement for a Dedicated or Private deployment evaluation.

[10:05] Maya: On encryption, Priya had asked earlier about KMS. We support both Redwood-managed KMS and BYOK (customer-managed keys) through AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations.
[10:18] Priya: For us, BYOK is preferred. Need to show key rotation policy and separation of duties — auditors ask for KMS logs and key rotation docs.
[10:26] Liam: BYOK flow: you provide a CMK in your cloud KMS; Redwood is granted a key usage policy and logs key usage via CloudTrail (or equivalent). We can deliver the CloudTrail/Crypto logs as evidence. Rotation is driven by your KMS policy; Redwood supports automatic rewrap when keys rotate. There's also an HSM-backed option for Private deployments.

[12:30] Jared: If we do BYOK, what about secret zero or key ingest? Are keys ever exported out of Atlas' control?
[12:37] Liam: No keys are exported. We only store wrapped keys and use your KMS to unwrap during runtime. For on-prem, HSM handles the unwrap on your side if you prefer. The transcript generator may have munged "wrap/unwrap" as "re-wrap" earlier in our docs, but the Trust Center diagrams show the exact lifecycle.

[15:00] Sofia: Evidence delivery — does Redwood provide a controls mapping (i.e., which Redwood artifact satisfies which SOC/ISO control)? That mapping is gold for our auditors.
[15:09] Maya: Yes — we have a controls matrix that maps Trust Center artifacts and system configurations to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls. We'll share the controls mapping spreadsheet but note that some controls require customer evidence (e.g., network segmentation at Atlas end).
[15:24] Priya: Great. Can you annotate which items are customer responsibility vs Redwood responsibility?
[15:29] Maya: We'll deliver a two-column mapping: Redwood artifacts (attestations, config exports, logs) and customer artifacts (network diagrams, internal policies).

[18:45] Jared: Slightly technical question — how do you handle KV cache and model-level traces for PII? We do not want model-level logs that include raw PII escaping into long-term logs.
[18:58] Liam: Good callout. We redact PII in transcript logs by default for hosted plans and store model traces separately with stricter access controls. For Dedicated/Private, you can disable model trace retention or route traces to an isolated bucket that you control. There's occasional noisy transcription that calls it "kay-vee cache" but it's the same KV cache concept — we can control what gets logged.

[22:10] Priya: Data residency — our EU customers' data must remain in EU regions. Does Redwood guarantee region-level residency for inference data and logs?
[22:22] Maya: Yes. For hosted we have region options and guarantee in-region processing and log storage when you select EU region. For stricter guarantees we recommend Redwood Private in your VPC or a Dedicated capacity in EU region with contractual data processing addendum.

[24:50] Sofia: One of our auditors asked about tamper evidence for logs. Do you support append-only logs or WORM storage for evidence exports?
[25:02] Liam: We support export into WORM-compliant object storage and can provide signed manifests and checksums for exported evidence bundles. Internally our audit store is append-only with retention locks for attestation artifacts.

[28:30] Priya: Are penetration test reports and change control docs available in Trust Center or do we request them?
[28:37] Maya: Pen test summaries and major change control summaries are in the Trust Center's "Reports" section — full reports are gated but we can provide executive summaries and redacted reports on request under NDA.

[31:00] Jared: Regarding SSO, we use Okta with group attributes. Is it possible to map an Okta group to an in-system RL role that only has read/list permissions for auditors?
[31:12] Liam: Absolutely — you can map Okta group to the "auditor" role. We support SCIM provisioning as well for automated user lifecycle. Sometimes the auto-transcription will truncate SCIM to 'skim' but it's the provisioning spec.

[34:20] Priya: Any time-limited access options for external auditors? They don't want permanent accounts.
[34:28] Maya: Yes — we can issue time-limited auditor tokens or invite auditors to the Trust Center with expiry. There's also a "one-time export" link if you prefer giving them a package rather than portal access.

[37:10] Sofia: A few nitty-gritty things auditors ask: evidence naming conventions, curation timestamps, and chain-of-custody — do you provide metadata per artifact?
[37:22] Liam: Each artifact includes metadata: generated_at, source, hash, and attachment to control IDs. The Trust Center UI surfaces those fields; the API returns them too for scripted evidence pulls.

[40:00] Priya: On the topic of encryption in transit — do you support mTLS for private deployments?
[40:07] Liam: For Private and Dedicated we support mTLS between clients and runtime, and between control plane components if desired. Hosted uses TLS with strong ciphers and we publish our cipher suite.

[43:30] Jared: For the PoC, we planned a small integration to exercise KMS BYOK and a log forwarder. What should we expect as minimal steps?
[43:40] Liam: Minimal PoC steps: 1) share SAML metadata and create an auditor test group; 2) provision a CMK for BYOK with a test policy; 3) configure log forwarder (we'll provide a small container) and send example events; 4) we'll validate audit fields and produce a short evidence bundle. Should be a couple days of hands-on with our SE assistance.

[47:10] Priya: Timeline — our SOC 2 window is starting mid-August. We need to have evidence flow and known responsibilities by end of July. Can we commit to the next checkpoints?
[47:22] Maya: Yes. Action plan: I'll send Trust Center invites and the attestation PDFs this week. Liam will provision sample artifacts for KMS & logs. Atlas to confirm in-scope systems. We can do a follow-up review in two weeks to validate PoC outputs.

[50:00] Sofia: One last question — if we later choose Dedicated vs Hosted for compliance reasons, how disruptive is migration for evidence lineage?
[50:12] Liam: Migration is supported; we retain artifact mappings and can map historical evidence to the new tenancy. There are some operational steps around keys and endpoints but we have a migration checklist for audits so lineage is preserved.

[53:00] Maya: Okay, recap of next steps: Maya send reports and Trust Center invite; Liam provide KMS/BYOK flow and sample logs; Jared/Sofia confirm RBAC matrix and residency requirements. Any objections?
[53:20] Priya: Sounds good.
[53:22] Jared: Agreed.
[53:24] Sofia: Thanks, all.
[54:00] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with the links.

End of transcript.
